_doc: Motion layers. AI clips animate the original plates (image-to-video, style preserved). Pending Wan clips use the 5-slot `shot` template; `prompt` is written by `python3 reelkit/clips.py compose <ep>` — never edit it by hand. Clips without `shot` were generated before the template and are frozen (their prompt is part of their cache key). Generate: clips.py gen <ep> (cache first).

template.style: Hand-made illustrated cut-paper collage animation. The picture keeps exactly the same drawing, ink linework, halftone grain, torn paper edges, aged cream paper texture and limited palette of deep red, ink black, mustard and cream as the input image. Every figure and object stays exactly as drawn, with the same face, clothing and proportions from the first frame to the last. Movement is slow, small and physically plausible, like a finely animated paper diorama lit by practical lights. Only the elements described above move; the rest of the collage stays perfectly still.

clips.prompt: A Soviet duty officer in an olive uniform and peaked cap sits with his back to us at a long analogue control console, facing an enormous glowing red world map that fills the upper wall of a dark underground command bunker. First, the red light across the world map slowly brightens and thin red tracking lines pulse outward across the continents. Then small indicator lamps along the console blink on one after another from left to right while the little green monitor screens shimmer softly. Then the officer lifts his head slightly toward the map and his shoulders tense, while he stays seated in the chair. Finally, a faint haze drifts through the red light near the ceiling pipes. Night inside a cramped Soviet early-warning bunker in 1983: riveted metal walls, exposed pipes and cables, wooden ceiling beams, worn steel desk panels with dials, switches and small round monitors, lit almost entirely by the deep red glow of the wall map. The map dominates the top half of the vertical frame; the officer and his chair sit in the lower centre, small against the console; dark machinery frames both sides and the floor fades into shadow at the bottom edge. Camera: slow steady push-in toward the officer's back, keeping the map centred. Hand-made illustrated cut-paper collage animation. Every figure and object stays exactly as drawn, with the same face, clothing and proportions from the first frame to the last. A middle-aged Soviet air-defence lieutenant colonel with swept-back reddish hair, in a dark uniform jacket with shoulder boards and medals, sits at a radar console resting his chin on his hand, deep in thought, his other hand near the switches. First, the red rotating beacon at the upper left pulses brighter and dimmer in a steady rhythm, washing the side of his face in red light. Then he draws one slow, heavy breath, his chest and shoulders rising and settling. Then his eyes narrow slightly as he weighs the decision, his face otherwise calm and unchanged. Finally, the green radar sweep on the round screen behind him turns once, slowly. A Soviet air-defence command post in 1983, built as a layered torn-paper collage: black-and-white printed machinery, fragments of an old map, olive-green panels and halftone shading with hot red accents. The officer fills the centre of the vertical frame from chest to head; the red beacon sits at the upper left, radar screens and gauges at the right, a torn strip of old map paper runs diagonally across the top left corner, and the console with knobs and cables fills the bottom of the frame. Camera: very slow push-in toward his face. Hand-made illustrated cut-paper collage animation. clips.prompt: A man's weathered hand rests on the receiver of a cream rotary telephone on a scratched red wooden desk, beneath a large round wall clock with a white face and black numerals. First, the fingers tighten slowly around the receiver. Then the hand lifts the receiver a few centimetres off its cradle and the coiled black cord stretches slightly. Then the hand pauses, holding the receiver just above the cradle, steady and deliberate. Finally, the dim red light on the wall breathes gently and fine dust floats through the air. A worn Soviet duty office late at night in 1983: peeling red and cream wallpaper, pinned newspaper clippings and torn paper scraps on the wall, a stack of papers and a pencil on the desk. The clock hangs in the upper centre of the vertical frame; the telephone sits on the desk in the lower middle with the hand entering from the right edge; the papers lie at the right of the desk and the dark desk front fills the bottom of the frame. An elderly couple sit at a small wooden kitchen table, seen from behind: a grey-haired man in a patterned red and cream knitted sweater on the left and a grey-haired woman with her hair in a bun, in a grey dress, on the right, with glasses of tea and a plate of biscuits between them. First, snow falls slowly past the dark window in front of the lit apartment blocks outside. Then the warm pendant lamp above the table sways very gently and its glow softly breathes. Then the man slowly lifts his glass of tea and sets it down on the table again. Finally, the woman leans slightly toward him, calm and close. A modest Soviet apartment kitchen on a winter night: lace curtains, patterned wallpaper, an old radio on a shelf, hanging utensils, a teapot, warm amber lamplight against the blue night outside. The window with lace curtains fills the upper middle of the vertical frame, the pendant lamp hangs at top centre, the couple and the table occupy the lower half with chairs at both sides, and the wooden floor runs along the bottom edge.
